metric_definitions.failure_recall_conservative: TP / all agreed reference failures; automatic abstentions and request errors are missed failures.
metric_definitions.failure_recall_decided: TP / (TP + decided FN); excludes automatic abstentions and request errors.
metric_definitions.decided_coverage: Automatic pass/fail decisions / all agreed reference pass/fail answers.
metric_definitions.scheduled_decided_coverage: Automatic pass/fail decisions on agreed references / all 120 frozen slots.
metric_definitions.false_positive_rate_decided: FP / (FP + TN); reference-pass automatic abstentions are excluded and separately disclosed.
metric_definitions.false_positive_rate_lower_bound: FP / all agreed reference passes; assumes no false-positive risk in abstentions.
metric_definitions.false_positive_rate_upper_bound: (FP + all undecided reference passes) / all agreed reference passes.
metric_definitions.gold_primary_type_coverage: Agreed single primary failure type / all agreed reference failures.
metric_definitions.classification_accuracy_detected_classif: Correct primary types / detected failures with an agreed single reference type; missing automatic types remain in denominator.
metric_definitions.classification_accuracy_compared_types: Correct / (correct + incorrect) primary types; excludes missing automatic types and nonclassifiable references.
metric_definitions.classification_accuracy_conservative_all: Verified correct primary types / all detected reference failures. Nonclassifiable reference types remain unverified, not known incorrect.
metric_definitions.joint_detection_and_classification_recal: Verified correctly detected and typed failures / all agreed reference failures.
metric_definitions.automatic_type_coverage_all_failures: Detected failures with an automatic primary type / all agreed reference failures, irrespective of reference-type agreement.

threshold_evaluation.classification_denominator_notice: The frozen JSON names the metric but omits its denominator. Existing AC3 service code uses correct categories / all detected reference failures; the earlier pilot draft uses detected failures with two agreed categories. Both are reported. The conservative all-detected check does not call unclassifiable reference types wrong; they are unverified. No post-result choice of the more favorable denominator establishes acceptance.

history_cluster_bootstrap.interpretation: The same 30 histories are resampled jointly for both scorers. Related synthetic histories are not a random population sample; these intervals describe observed-cohort resampling variability, not external generalisation.

baseline.execution: offline replay on the same new Astra MAX saved answers; no model call

provenance.reference_review_model_provenance: Independent AI agent declarations retained; not OpenAI API transport receipts and not independently authenticated human review.

limitations: The user reports two people independently verified every new AI-assisted reference judgment. Original AI opinions remain preserved; identities and blindness to automatic scores are not independently established. Human approval does not establish complete AC3 acceptance.
Both reviewers and the candidate judge share the Astra model family; correlated errors remain possible despite independently blinded review.
Thirty reused, related synthetic histories are a descriptive cohort, not a population-random sample or unseen external benchmark.
A primary failure type is verified only when both reviewers independently identify the same actual error. Unclassifiable failures remain in answer-level denominators.
Zero agreed positive failures for a type means sensitivity for that type is unmeasured, not perfect or zero.
Conditional classification rates can overstate whole-cohort diagnostic performance; all-failure joint coverage and conservative all-detected rates are shown alongside them.
This comparison isolates scoring on the same saved answers. It is not a target-model improvement claim relative to archived Luna experiments.
A single target response per question does not establish between-run sampling stability. Cluster intervals keep within-history questions together but do not resolve cohort-selection bias.
With no observed false positives, a resampling interval can collapse to zero. This does not bound the false-positive risk in unseen cases or establish zero population risk.
